mainTopic: How a woman checks herself around תשמיש (בית שמאי and בית הלל, טהרות, a lost cloth), the ban on daytime relations and its sources, and related lists of hated behaviors.
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where בית שמאי require a woman to check herself before and after every act of תשמיש in a night. בית הלל say one check before the first act and one after the last act is enough. They argue over whether blood could be hidden by semen, and רבי יוחנן's teacher רבי יהושע sides with בית שמאי. רבי זירא learns that a בעל נפש should check between acts, but רבא says these checks are only for טהרות, and a ברייתא confirms that she is permitted to her husband as long as he left her with a חזקת טהרה. רב rules that if her checking cloth was lost, she must check again, and רבא explains why a lost cloth is different from one she simply hasn't looked at yet. רבי יוחנן then forbids relations during the day. רב המנונא and ריש לקיש each bring a different פסוק as the source. The גמרא shows what each one learns from the other's פסוק: the angel named 'לילה' and free will in יראת שמים, and בן סירא's list of hated behaviors. The amud ends with רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's list of four things ה׳ hates, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How many examinations are needed in one night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: בית שמאי require two עדים for every act of תשמיש, or lamplight; בית הלל say two עדים for the whole night are enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: The Sages taught: Even though they said that one who has intercourse by the light of a lamp is acting disgracefully, בית שמאי say: She needs two examination cloths for every act of intercourse, or she should have intercourse by lamplight. And בית הלל say: Two examination cloths are enough for her for the whole night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that lays out a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל. The question is how often a woman must check herself when there are several acts of תשמיש in one night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי want a check before and after each act, or else lamplight as the other option, even though lamplight is normally called מגונה. בית הלל say one check before the first act and one after the last act is enough for the whole night. The rest of the sugya is the argument over this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'witnesses'; here, the cloths a woman uses to check herself for blood
By the light of a lamp

phrases.english: GEMARA
The Sages taught:
Even though they said
one who has intercourse by the light of a lamp
this is disgraceful,
Beit Shammai say:
she needs two examination cloths
phrases.notes: עדים literally means 'witnesses': the cloth 'tells' whether there was blood. Two means one check before and one after.

phrases.english: for each act of intercourse,
or she should have intercourse by lamplight.
And Beit Hillel say:
it is enough for her with two examination cloths
for the entire night.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ הַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ לְאוֹר הַנֵּר הֲרֵי זֶה מְגוּנֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's mention of בית שמאי and lamplight.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: two עדים per act of תשמיש, or lamplight. בית הלל: two עדים for the whole night.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי want a check around every act. בית הלל are fine with one check before the first act and one after the last act.

steps.title: בית שמאי worry that blood could be hidden
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי challenge בית הלל: a tiny drop of blood from the first act could be covered by semen from the second act and go unnoticed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: בית שמאי said to בית הלל: According to your view, we should worry that she might see a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed during the first act, and semen from the second act will cover it.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי attack בית הלל's position. They explain why one check at the end of the night is not good enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no check between acts, a tiny drop of blood from the first act could get covered by semen from the second act. Then the final check would miss it, and she would wrongly think she is טהורה. This is the reason behind בית שמאי's requirement to check after every act.

keyTerms.meaning: According to your words or view
A drop of blood as small as a mustard seed

phrases.english: It is taught:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל:
phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:
According to your words,
let us be concerned that perhaps she will see
a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed
during the first act of intercourse,
and semen will cover it
during the second act of intercourse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל: לְדִבְרֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית שמאי's reasoning against בית הלל's ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's rule that two עדים for the whole night are enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a check between acts, blood from the first act could be hidden by the second act's semen and missed at the final check.

steps.title: בית הלל answer: your view has the same problem
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל reply that even with a check after each act, the blood could be squashed and hidden before the check.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: Even according to your view, we should worry that while the saliva is still in the mouth, perhaps it got squashed and disappeared.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל turn the challenge back on בית שמאי. They argue that the same worry applies even to בית שמאי's own rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if she checks right after every act, the semen of that same act could cover a drop of blood before she checks. So checking after each act does not fully remove the worry either. If בית שמאי accept that risk, why not accept it across the whole night?

keyTerms.meaning: Even according to your view; a reply showing the other side has the same problem
Saliva; used here as a picture

steps.confusionAlert: The 'saliva in the mouth' is not about actual saliva. It is a picture for blood that is still inside the body and gets squashed and hidden before she can check.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them:
Even according to your words,
let us be concerned that while the saliva is still in the mouth,
phrases.notes: This is a picture: while the blood is still inside, before she has a chance to check.

phrases.english: perhaps it was squashed and disappeared.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל: אַף לְדִבְרֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 with a counter-challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's claim that checking after each act solves the problem.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood can be hidden by the semen of the very same act, so בית שמאי's rule faces the same risk.

steps.title: בית שמאי: once is not like twice
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that blood squashed by one act is not like blood squashed by two acts, so their worry is stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to them: Because blood squashed once cannot be compared to blood squashed twice.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי defend their position against בית הלל's counter-challenge. They point to a difference in how serious the risk is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי admit that one act could hide some blood. But two acts on top of the blood make it much more likely to be completely hidden. So the risk in בית הלל's view is greater, and checking after each act is still needed.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's final point: one squashing is a small risk, but two squashings are a real risk. That is why they demand a check after every act, while בית הלל are satisfied with checks at the start and end of the night.

phrases.english: They said to them:
phrases.notes: Here it is בית שמאי answering בית הלל.

phrases.english: Because it is not comparable:
squashed one time,
to squashed two times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית הלל's counter-challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since one act can also hide blood, בית שמאי's concern seemed to apply equally to their own rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two acts covering the blood is much more likely to hide it than one act, so the concern is stronger in בית הלל's case.

steps.title: רבי יהושע sides with בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע agrees with בית שמאי. His students complain that this is very strict, and he answers that strictness in this world brings long life in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהושע said, "I see בית שמאי's view as correct." His students said, "רבי, how heavy you have made things for us!" He answered, "Better that I make things heavy for you in this world, so that your days will be made long in the World to Come."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע decides that בית שמאי's strict view, a check for every act, makes more sense. His students push back because it is hard, and he explains why it is worth it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the back-and-forth in steps 2-4, רבי יהושע is convinced by בית שמאי's last point: blood squashed by two acts is much harder to see. His answer to the students is a play on words. The root ארך, 'long', is used both for 'making it long and heavy for you' and for 'lengthening your days'.

keyTerms.meaning: I see the words of (someone) as correct; I agree with them
You have made it long and heavy for us; you have been very strict with us

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי.
phrases.english: I see the words of בית שמאי as correct.
His students said to him:
Rebbi, how heavy you have made it for us!
phrases.notes: Literally 'how long you have made it on us'. The root ארך ('long') sets up his reply.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: מוּטָב שֶׁאַאֲרִיךְ עֲלֵיכֶם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
phrases.english: He said to them: Better that I make it heavy for you in this world,
so that your days will be lengthened in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: רוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing בית שמאי's final answer in step 4, רבי יהושע sides with them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע rules like בית שמאי: she must check between each act.

steps.title: רבי זירא: a careful person should not repeat without a check
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא learns from both views that a בעל נפש should not have relations a second time without a check in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: From the words of all of them we learn that a בעל נפש should not have relations and then repeat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא draws a practical lesson from the whole מחלוקת: a person who wants to be extra careful should check between each act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא reads the מחלוקת as being only about what is allowed בדיעבד, after the fact. Even בית הלל would agree that the ideal is a check between acts, so a בעל נפש should act that way from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: From the words of all of them we learn; a lesson both sides would accept
A careful, pious person who takes on extra strictness
He should not have relations and then repeat

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
From the words of all of them we learn,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means both בית שמאי and בית הלל.

phrases.english: a pious person should not have relations and repeat.
phrases.notes: He means not repeat without a check in between.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the מחלוקת itself to a practical lesson for a careful person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל נפש should not have relations twice without a check in between.

steps.title: רבא: the whole discussion is only about pure items
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רבי זירא. Even a careful person may repeat, because the ברייתא about checks only deals with a woman who handles טהרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He may have relations and repeat. When that ברייתא was taught, it was about טהרות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רבי זירא's lesson by limiting the ברייתא from step 1 to a different topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says the checks of בית שמאי and בית הלל were never about whether she is allowed to her husband. They are about a woman who handles pure items and must know she is not making them טמא. So nothing can be learned about the husband, and even a בעל נפש may repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually pure items such as food that must be kept pure

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the checks don't matter. He is saying they matter for טהרות, not for whether she is allowed to her husband.

phrases.english: Rava said: He may have relations and repeat,
because when that ברייתא was taught, it was about pure items.
phrases.notes: 'That ברייתא' is the one from step 1 with בית שמאי and בית הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בּוֹעֵל וְשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי זירא's lesson in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי זירא's practical lesson for a בעל נפש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי זירא assumed the ברייתא was about her being allowed to her husband, but it is only about טהרות.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא: permitted to her husband
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the checks are only for טהרות, but she is allowed to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: When was this said? For pure items. But to her husband, she is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says just what רבא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly limits the checking rules to טהרות and says that for her husband she is permitted without them. This backs רבא's reading over רבי זירא's.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? (sets the limits of a rule)

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא:
In what case was this said? For pure items,
but to her husband, she is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's view from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the checks are only for טהרות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says the rule is for טהרות, but she is permitted to her husband.

steps.title: Limit on the leniency: how her husband left her
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that she is allowed without asking only if her husband left her in a חזקת טהרה. If he left her טמאה, she stays טמאה until she tells him she is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when was this said? When he left her with a presumption of purity. But if he left her with a presumption of impurity, she always stays in that status until she tells him, "I am pure."
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now limits its own leniency: it depends on her status when her husband last left her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה means we assume things stay as they were last known. If she was טהורה when he left, we assume she still is. If she was טמאה, we assume she still is, so he needs her to say she is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption that she is pure
A presumption that she is impure
He left her (when he went away)

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, a woman is allowed to her husband without checks before and after תשמיש. Those checks are for טהרות. But if she was last known to be טמאה, he must wait until she says "טהורה אני".
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a חזקה sets the default: her last known status holds until something changes it.

phrases.english: And in what case was this said?
phrases.notes: 'This' is the leniency that she is permitted to her husband.

phrases.english: When he left her with a presumption of purity,
but if he left her with a presumption of impurity,
she always stays in her presumed status,
until she says to him, "I am pure."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים — שֶׁהִנִּיחָהּ בְּחֶזְקַת טׇהֳרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and limits the leniency from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency applies only if her husband left her with a חזקת טהרה. If he left her with a חזקת טמאה, she stays טמאה until she says she is pure.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: She is permitted to her husband without checks only when her last known status was טהורה.

steps.title: A lost checking cloth means she must check again
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if a woman checked with a cloth and the cloth got lost, she may not have relations until she checks again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רבי חייא בר אשי, who said in the name of רב: If she checked with a cloth and the cloth got lost, she may not have relations until she checks again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רב about a woman whose checking cloth got lost right after she checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She did check, but she never saw the result. Maybe there was blood on the lost cloth. So רב says the lost check does not count, and she must check again before relations.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloth used for checking for blood

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
If she checked with a cloth and it got lost,
she is forbidden to have relations until she checks again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of checks around relations with a new case: a check whose cloth was lost.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A check whose cloth was lost does not count. She must check again before relations.

steps.title: Even with the cloth, she doesn't know the result yet
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא argues that even if the cloth were not lost, she would have relations without knowing the result. So why should losing it change anything?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא challenges this: If the cloth were still here, wouldn't she have relations even though she doesn't know yet what is on it? So now too, let her have relations!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילא attacks רב's rule. He compares the lost cloth to a cloth she still has but has not looked at yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally she checks at night and only looks at the cloth the next day, and she still may have relations that night. In both cases she has relations without knowing the result. So רבי אילא asks why losing the cloth should forbid her.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges it, raises a strong objection
If it were here (if the cloth still existed)
Even though she does not know

phrases.english: Rabbi Ila challenges this:
If the cloth were here,
phrases.notes: He means if the cloth had not been lost and she would only look at it the next day.

phrases.english: wouldn't she have relations,
even though she does not know what is on it?
Now too, let her have relations!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אִילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's rule from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a lost cloth forbids relations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A cloth she still has but has not checked also leaves her not knowing, and she is allowed. So the lost cloth should be allowed too.

steps.title: An existing cloth can still give proof; a lost one cannot
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a cloth that still exists can prove later what happened, but a lost cloth can never prove anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: This one has its proof still existing, and that one does not have its proof existing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רב by showing a real difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cloth still exists, they will look at it the next day. If they find blood, they will know they sinned and can bring a קרבן חטאת to fix it. With a lost cloth they will never know, so they can never fix it. That is why רב forbids relations before a new check.
steps.whatToRemember: A check only helps if its result can be known. A lost cloth can never show if they need atonement, so she must check again.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
This one, her proof still exists,
phrases.notes: This is the woman who still has her cloth and will look at it later.

phrases.english: and that one, her proof does not exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: זוֹ מוֹכִיחָהּ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אילא's challenge from step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases are the same because in both she does not know the result at the time of relations.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ: an existing cloth can still show the truth later so they can fix a mistake. A lost cloth never can.

steps.title: No relations during the day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a person may not have relations during the daytime.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A person is forbidden to have relations during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: רבי יוחנן's rule against relations by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new rule, separate from the checking cloth. The next steps will look for the פסוק that teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: To have marital relations (literally 'use his bed')

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is forbidden for a person to have relations during the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָסוּר לָאָדָם שֶׁיְּשַׁמֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic; not connected to the checking cloth discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations during the day are forbidden.

steps.title: The source: night is for conception
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא brings a פסוק from איוב showing that night is the time for conception, not day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: What is the source? As it says: 'Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night on which it was said: a man-child is conceived.' Night is given for conception, and day is not given for conception.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא gives a פסוק to support רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, birth is linked to 'day' but conception is linked to 'night'. From this he learns that conception, and so relations, belong to the night and not the day.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said: What is the verse?
As it is said: “Let the day perish on which I was born,”
“and the night on which it was said: a man-child is conceived.”
Night is given for conception,
and day is not given for conception.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for רבי יוחנן's rule in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The ban on relations by day
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 3:3, which links conception to night

steps.title: A different source: 'He who despises his ways'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns the same rule from a different פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: From here: 'He who despises his ways shall die.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives his own source for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not spell out how this פסוק teaches the rule. רש״י explains that in daylight he might see something he dislikes in his wife and come to despise her.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: From here:
“He who despises his ways shall die.”

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same rule from step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The ban on relations by day

steps.title: What does ריש לקיש do with the night verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ריש לקיש uses the פסוק from איוב, since he did not use it for this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש, what does he learn from this פסוק used for רבי יוחנן's rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a standard question: if ריש לקיש did not use the איוב פסוק for this rule, what does he learn from it? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every פסוק teaches something. If ריש לקיש didn't take the איוב verse as the source, it must be teaching him something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish,
this verse of Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: This is the איוב verse that רב המנונא used in step 14 for רבי יוחנן's rule.

phrases.english: what does he learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, הַאי קְרָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about ריש לקיש's view after he chose a different פסוק in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ריש לקיש learns from the איוב פסוק

steps.title: The verse teaches about the angel named 'Night'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש uses the איוב פסוק for רבי חנינא בר פפא's teaching: the angel in charge of conception is called 'לילה', and he asks ה׳ what will become of each drop.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what רבי חנינא בר פפא taught: The angel in charge of conception is named 'Night'. He takes the drop, stands it before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and says: Master of the world, what will be with this drop? Strong or weak? Wise or foolish? Rich or poor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ריש לקיש reads the איוב verse as a story about an angel, not as a rule about the time of relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, 'the night that said a man-child is conceived' is the angel named 'לילה' who speaks about the conception. So the word 'night' is a name, not a time of day, and the פסוק is free for this lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
The drop (of seed) from which a child is formed

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'לילה' is the angel's name, not the time of night. That is exactly why ריש לקיש cannot use this פסוק to teach about relations at night.

phrases.aramaic: מִבָּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְדָרֵישׁ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: He needs it for what Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa taught,
as Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa taught:
That angel who is in charge of conception
is named “Night,”
and he takes the drop
and stands it before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
and says before Him:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, טִפָּה זוֹ מָה תְּהֵא עָלֶיהָ?
phrases.english: Master of the world, what will become of this drop?
Strong or weak?

phrases.aramaic: חָכָם אוֹ טִיפֵּשׁ? עָשִׁיר אוֹ עָנִי?
phrases.english: Wise or foolish? Rich or poor?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִבָּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְדָרֵישׁ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש uses the איוב פסוק for רבי חנינא בר פפא's teaching that the angel of conception is named 'לילה'.

steps.title: The angel never asks if the child will be righteous or wicked
steps.stepSummary: The angel 'לילה' asks about many things for the coming child, but not whether he will be a צדיק or a רשע. That follows רבי חנינא: everything is in Heaven's hands except יראת שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the angel does not ask whether the child will be wicked or righteous. This follows רבי חנינא, who said: Everything is in the hands of Heaven except fear of Heaven, as it says: 'And now, Israel, what does ה׳ your God ask of you other than to fear...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more detail to the angel's question from Step 17: he does not ask whether the child will be good or bad. It explains why using רבי חנינא's famous teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ decides a person's strength, wisdom, wealth and so on before birth. Whether he will fear Heaven is left to his own choice. The proof is that ה׳ 'asks' us to fear Him, and you only ask for something a person is free to give or hold back.

keyTerms.meaning: Everything is in the hands of Heaven (decided by ה׳)
Fear of Heaven, a person's own religious choice

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the key sources in חז"ל for בחירה חפשית (free will). A person's moral path is not decided before he is born.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'everything is in Heaven's hands' means a person has no choice at all. The whole point is the exception: whether you fear Heaven is up to you.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ רָשָׁע אוֹ צַדִּיק לָא קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: But 'wicked or righteous' he does not say,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the angel 'לילה' from the last step, who asks ה׳ about each drop.

phrases.english: in line with Rabbi Chanina.
As Rabbi Chanina said:
Everything is in the hands of Heaven,
except for fear of Heaven,
as it is said: "And now, Israel,
what does ה׳ your God ask of you
other than to fear, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ רָשָׁע אוֹ צַדִּיק לָא קָאָמַר, כִּדְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the angel's question in Step 17 and explains it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angel does not ask whether the child will be righteous or wicked, because fear of Heaven is left to human choice (רבי חנינא).

steps.title: How רבי יוחנן gets two lessons from the איוב verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן agrees the איוב פסוק teaches about the angel, but its unusual word order teaches a second lesson: night is for conception, day is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: if the פסוק only meant the angel, it should have written 'a man was conceived.' Why does it say 'conceived, a man'? To teach that night is given for conception, and day is not given for conception.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יוחנן can use the איוב פסוק both for the angel and for the rule against daytime relations. The odd word order shows that the פסוק carries an extra lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש used the איוב פסוק only for the angel. רבי יוחנן says the order 'הורה גבר' instead of 'גבר הורה' points to a second lesson. Putting 'conceived' first, right after 'night', teaches that conception belongs to night and not to day.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if the verse only meant that)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how רבי יוחנן's ruling from Step 13 rests on the איוב פסוק while still keeping the teaching about the angel.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan holds:
if so, let the verse write "a man was conceived";
what is the meaning of "conceived is a man"?
Night is given for conception,
and day is not given for conception.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אִם כֵּן נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having shown how ריש לקיש uses the איוב פסוק, the גמרא now explains how רבי יוחנן reads the same פסוק to get both lessons.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can רבי יוחנן use the איוב פסוק for the daytime rule if it teaches about the angel?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The unusual word order 'הורה גבר' adds a second lesson: night, not day, is for conception.

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן learn from ריש לקיש's verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the mirror question: since רבי יוחנן learns the rule from איוב, what does he do with the משלי פסוק that ריש לקיש used?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, what does he learn from this פסוק of ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן does with ריש לקיש's פסוק from משלי. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 asked what ריש לקיש does with the איוב פסוק. Now the same question is turned around. The assumption is that every פסוק must teach something, so if רבי יוחנן does not use it for the daytime rule, he must use it for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he learn (expound) from it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan,
this verse of Reish Lakish,
phrases.notes: This is the משלי פסוק from Step 15, "בוזה דרכיו ימות" (משלי 19:16).

phrases.english: what does he learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, הַאי קְרָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 16's question, now asked about רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש's פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson does רבי יוחנן take from the משלי פסוק, since he does not use it for the daytime rule?

steps.title: בן סירא's list of people who are hated
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses the משלי פסוק for the teaching in ספר בן סירא, which lists three kinds of people that are hated and a fourth that is not loved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what is written in ספר בן סירא: Three I have hated, and a fourth I have not loved: a minister who hangs around drinking houses (some say: who chatters there; some say: who gets angry there); one who sets up his home at the highest point of the city; one who holds his organ while urinating; and one who walks into his friend's house suddenly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק about 'one who despises his ways' as pointing to the kinds of bad behavior listed in ספר בן סירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of daytime relations, the 'disgraceful ways' in the פסוק are these behaviors. For the first item, three versions of the wording are given: נרגל (frequents), נרגן (chatters), נרגז (gets angry), all about a minister in drinking houses.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the verse) for a different lesson
The book of Ben Sira, a book of wisdom sayings
The highest point of the city

phrases.english: He needs it for what is written
in the book of Ben Sira:
Three I have hated,
and a fourth I have not loved:
a minister who frequents drinking houses,
and some say: "a minister who chatters,"
and some say: "a minister who is short-tempered."
And one who sets his dwelling at the heights of the city,
phrases.notes: Here שבת doesn't mean the day of rest. It means a dwelling place, from the root of 'sitting' or 'living'.

phrases.english: and one who holds his organ while urinating,
and one who enters his friend's house suddenly.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לִכְדִכְתִיב בְּסֵפֶר בֶּן סִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן uses the משלי פסוק for בן סירא's list of disgraceful behaviors, not for the daytime rule.

steps.title: Even entering your own house suddenly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that the last item, entering a house suddenly, applies even to one's own home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: And even into his own house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן widens the last item on בן סירא's list. You should not walk in without warning even into your own home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the problem is only walking into someone else's house. רבי יוחנן teaches that a person should give notice even before entering his own home.

keyTerms.meaning: And even into his own house

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן learns the ban on daytime relations from the word order in איוב ('הורה גבר'). ריש לקיש's פסוק in משלי is used by רבי יוחנן for בן סירא's list of hated behaviors, which he extends to entering even your own home suddenly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a practical lesson in דרך ארץ: give notice before walking in, even into your own house.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And even into his own house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְבֵיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the last item of בן סירא's list from Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not enter suddenly even into one's own house.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's four hated things, first two items
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי lists four things the הקדוש ברוך הוא hates and that he himself does not love. The first two are entering one's house suddenly and holding the אמה while urinating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי said: There are four things that the Holy One, Blessed be He, hates, and I do not love them either. One is a person who walks into his own house suddenly, and of course into his friend's house. Another is a person who holds his אמה while urinating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar teaching from רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, a list of four things ה׳ hates. This amud gives the first two items, and the list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list backs up what רבי יוחנן just said in Step 22. Entering suddenly is a problem even in your own home, and with someone else's home it is even more obvious. The second item, holding the אמה while urinating, repeats an item already on בן סירא's list from Step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: and needless to say; all the more so

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the idea of not entering suddenly, even into one's own house, is not only רבי יוחנן's own reading. It also appears in רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's teaching.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׂוֹנְאָן,
phrases.english: Four things the Holy One, Blessed be He, hates,
and I do not love them:
one who enters his own house suddenly,
and needless to say, his friend's house,
and one who holds the organ and urinates,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׂוֹנְאָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel teaching that agrees with רבי יוחנן in Step 22: entering suddenly is a problem even in one's own home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הקדוש ברוך הוא hates (1) entering one's house suddenly, and all the more so another's house, and (2) holding the אמה while urinating. The list continues with two more items.
